title: Agent-intrusion synthetic replay corpus event (#154 phase 1)
description: One ordered event in the synthetic replay corpus. See README.md for the full design rationale and safety constraints -- this schema only enforces shape, not the safety rules (no real indicators, TEST-NET-only addresses, etc.), which validate_corpus.py checks separately since JSON Schema can't express 'this string must not look like a real secret.'

event_id.description: Stable identifier, also this event's ordering key within a phase-tie -- corpus.jsonl's own row order is the authoritative timeline order, this ID is for cross-referencing in docs/tests only.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 UTC. Ordered ascending across the whole corpus, matching the campaign's own day-by-day structure -- validate_corpus.py checks strict monotonicity.

phase.description: The 8 phases #154 required, plus 'benign' for near-neighbor control events that are not part of the attack chain at all (is_benign is true for these; is_benign can also be true within a non-benign phase for an event that merely resembles that phase's technique -- see README.md).

trust_boundary.description: The boundary this event's technique crosses, in APIARY's own terms (e.g. 'honeypot-session -> local-filesystem-recon'), not a generic label -- matches docs/agent-intrusion-threat-model.md's own per-area boundary language.

sensor.description: Which real APIARY sensor/source this event's 'raw' field is shaped like (cowrie, suricata, dashboard-audit, ci-workflow, etc.) -- phase 2's decoder is expected to consume raw sensor-shaped JSON, so this corpus provides realistic input, not an abstract description.

encoding_layer.description: What phase 2's decoder needs to peel back before the payload is human/rule readable. 'none' for events with no encoding at all (most recon/discovery events -- encoding is concentrated in the c2/exfil phases, matching the real campaign's own reported shape).

is_benign.description: True for near-neighbor control events: same sensor, similar surface shape, but not part of the attack chain (or, within an attack-chain phase, a technique that merely resembles it) -- these exist to measure false positives per #154's own corpus requirement ('include benign near-neighbors to measure false positives'). expected_findings.should_escalate must be false whenever this is true.

raw.description: A realistic, sensor-shaped JSON blob -- what phase 2's decoder would actually receive from that sensor in production. Entirely synthetic: TEST-NET addresses only (RFC 5737: 192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24), obviously-fake credential/token strings, no real hostnames or copied campaign IOCs.

should_escalate.description: Ground truth for phase 3's criticality rules: should this event (in the context of the events before it in this corpus) contribute to a raised campaign severity? Individual early-phase events are frequently false here even in the non-benign phases -- matching #154's own framing that isolated low-signal events are the point, not any single event being independently alarming.

decoded_summary.description: Ground truth for phase 2's decoder: a human-readable summary of what should come out the other end after decoding 'raw' (empty string if encoding_layer is 'none' and no decoding step applies).

matched_rule.description: Ground truth for phase 3: the deterministic criticality-rule identifier (once phase 3 defines them) this event is expected to match, or null if none. Left as free text/null in this phase-1 corpus since phase 3's rule set doesn't exist yet -- validate_corpus.py only checks the field is present and typed correctly, not that it names a real rule.

notes.description: What real campaign step (if any) this event is a synthetic analog of, and why it's shaped the way it is. Required on every event -- this corpus is a reviewable artifact, not just machine input.
